elements.evidence: Rendered § 12.4 now reads "Customer may solicit, hire, or employ Vendor employees without restriction." The one-sided bar ("shall not solicit, hire, or employ ... during the term or for twenty-four months afterward") is gone, and no other cited provision imposes a solicitation restraint on Customer; § 12.3 affirmatively confirms no no-hire commitment. Deterministic operation gate and element-coverage gate both pass.

No non-solicit covenant survives in the rendered text at all, so there is no mutual restraint; § 12.4 is a one-way permission in Customer's favour. Not a defect on the preferred path, but the fallback checklist is therefore incomplete.

elements.element: The restriction covers only personnel directly involved in the Services.
elements.evidence: No restriction exists in the rendered language to be scoped to Services personnel; the fallback scope limitation is absent (irrelevant given the preferred path is taken).

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months after the person's involvement ends.
elements.evidence: Deterministic check "non-solicit duration ≤ 12 months" returned "number not found" — correct, because no covenant with a duration remains. The fallback's 12-month-from-end-of-involvement anchor is not present in operative text.

elements.element: General advertisements are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Deterministic check "general-solicitation carve-out present" is false; § 12.4 contains no carve-out language because no covenant remains. § 12.3's "hiring any person who responds to general recruitment" is a Customer freedom statement, not a carve-out from a mutual covenant.

elements.element: Unsolicited approaches are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: No unsolicited-approach carve-out appears in operative text; it is only mentioned in the margin comment as a reserved negotiating fallback, and a promise in the comment does not count.

elements.element: The restriction does not prohibit hiring.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: there is no restriction, and § 12.4 expressly permits Customer to "hire, or employ" Vendor employees, so no hiring prohibition exists. The original no-hire ("hire, or employ ... regardless of how the employee applies") has been deleted.
Duplicate-safe restatement: no mutual covenant is drafted; the fallback level cannot be certified complete.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the sole preferred element (no non-solicitation restriction on Customer) is satisfied by the rewritten § 12.4, which removes the solicit/hire/employ bar and the 24-month tail in operative words rather than only in the comment.

The original clause was in walk-away territory (express no-hire, all Vendor employees, term plus 24 months, and an anti-carve-out phrase "regardless of how the employee applies"), so a redline rather than a rationale note is correctly chosen; the claimed "deviation" status is verified.

Fallback level is incomplete (no mutual, involvement-limited, 12-month covenant with general-advertisement and unsolicited-approach carve-outs), but that is immaterial because completeness at either level suffices and the preferred level is met.

Minimality holds: the edit touches only § 12.4, adds no survival tail, damages category, procedure, or notice mechanic, and does not import anything outside the preferred checklist. Replacing the sentence with a short permissive statement instead of striking § 12.4 outright is a mild redundancy with § 12.3's existing no-hire acknowledgment; if the counterparty objects to belt-and-braces language, simple deletion of § 12.4 would be equally compliant.

Intent is preserved: § 12.3's favourable Customer freedoms and no-hire acknowledgment are retained unchanged, the edit removes rather than creates the internal conflict, no defined term is orphaned, and the numbering/cross-references are intact (§ 12.4 remains occupied, so no dangling reference).
The comment correctly states what changed, cites the playbook position, and offers the mutual 12-month fallback without lecturing; tone and length are within guidance.
Note for the drafter: the separate non-compete text at p0046 is a distinct commercial term and is properly left to its own rule, so there is no double-flagging of the same term.
